governed_construct: A TypeScript interface declaration (InterfaceDeclaration node: `interface Name {...}`, with or without export/default/declare modifiers, at top level or nested in a namespace or ambient module). Each declared interface name is one instance. Type aliases, classes, and text inside strings, template literals or comments are not instances.
interpretation: The rule requires every interface name to be 'I' followed by a PascalCase name: a capital I, then an uppercase letter, then only letters and digits (regex on the name: ^I[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$). Conforming: IUserService, IRepository, IButtonProps. Violating: names without the I prefix (UserService, Response, OrderRepository), a lowercase prefix (iLogger), I followed by a lowercase letter (IapiResponse, which is not PascalCase after the prefix), and names containing underscores (IPayment_gateway). Generic parameters are not part of the name. Interface declarations nested in namespaces or declare-module blocks count. A file with no interface declarations (only type aliases or classes, even if named like interfaces) is NOT_APPLICABLE. Interface-like text produced inside string or template literals is code generation output, not a declaration, and is ignored.
